mainTopic: How much discharge or semen causes טומאה (for a זב, the man who emits semen, and one who touches it), and a new משנה on newborns' laws.
overview: This amud starts by finishing a question about a non-Jewish זבה who converted after her urine had started to move inside her. The question ends in תיקו. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that זוב and שכבת זרע make impure 'in any amount.' שמואל says a זב needs enough discharge to seal the opening, following רבי נתן in the name of רבי ישמעאל, a view the חכמים rejected. The גמרא shows how each side uses every phrase of the פסוקים in ויקרא 15. Together they teach that two sightings bring טומאה, three bring a קרבן, the discharge must leave the body, and the discharge itself is impure. Next, רב חנילאי rules that semen makes the man who emits it impure in any amount, but someone who touches it needs a lentil-size. The גמרא defends this against a משנה and a ברייתא, and explains the ברייתא's comparison of semen with a שרץ. רב פפא then shows that the toucher's amount depends on a תנאים dispute about how much of a comparison carries over. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן suggests a different source verse, and both versions turn out to have been taught. Finally, a new משנה begins, listing laws that apply to a baby girl and a baby boy from their very first days.

steps.title: She went down and immersed before the urine came out — what is the law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a question it started earlier. A non-Jewish זבה felt her urine start to move, then immersed for conversion before it came out. What is her status?
steps.simpleTranslation: And she went down and immersed — what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question it began just before this. A non-Jewish זבה felt her urine start to move inside her. Then she immersed to convert before it came out, and the גמרא asks what the law is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Urine of a זבה is impure. Here the urine started moving while she was a non-Jew, but it left her body after she converted. The question is which moment counts, and the next step spells out exactly why this is a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: She went down (into the מקוה) and immersed. Here it means immersing for conversion.
'What is it?' It asks what the law is in this case.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a question that started before this section. 'She' is the non-Jewish זבה who felt her urine begin to move. She is not a new person.

phrases.english: And she went down and immersed — what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'She' is the non-Jewish זבה from the question just before. She immersed to convert before the urine came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the case of a question started before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a non-Jewish זבה who felt her urine move before converting, and then converted, impure when the urine comes out?

steps.title: Why it is a doubt: Torah-level impurity versus rabbinic impurity
steps.stepSummary: Even if we normally go by the moment of עקירה, maybe that rule only applies to a Jewish woman, whose impurity is from the Torah. A non-Jewish זבה, whose impurity is only rabbinic, may be different. Or perhaps there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say we go by the moment the urine was uprooted inside, even though she could still hold it in. That may only be true for a Jewish woman, who is impure by Torah law. But a non-Jewish זבה, who is impure only by rabbinic law, may not follow that rule. Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two sides of the question. Maybe the rule of 'going by the uprooting' applies only to Torah-level impurity. Or maybe it applies the same way to rabbinic impurity too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The starting point is that we go by the moment of עקירה, even though she could still hold the urine in. The new idea is that this strict approach might be limited to a Jewish woman, who is impure דאורייתא. A non-Jewish זבה is only impure דרבנן, so perhaps the חכמים did not apply the uprooting rule to her.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Uprooting.' The moment the fluid starts to move inside the body, before it comes out.
We go by the moment of uprooting.
That she is able to hold them (the urine) in.
From the Torah / from the חכמים (rabbinic).
A non-Jewish woman who has had a זיבה discharge. She is impure only by rabbinic law.
'There is no difference.' Both cases follow the same rule.

phrases.english: If you say
that we go by the uprooting,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמָצֵי נָקֵיט לְהוּ —
phrases.english: even though she is able to hold it in —
phrases.notes: 'It' means the urine.

phrases.english: that applies to a Jewish woman
who is impure by Torah law,
but a non-Jewish זבה
who is impure by rabbinic law — not,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר בָּתַר עֲקִירָה אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the question asked in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule of going by עקירה apply to a non-Jewish זבה, whose impurity is only rabbinic, the same way it applies to a Jewish woman?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle the question, so it declares תיקו and leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether the uprooting rule applies to rabbinic impurity. So neither side wins, and the doubt remains.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it stand.' The question stays unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: Even if we go by the moment of עקירה, it is left unresolved whether that rule applies to a non-Jewish זבה, whose impurity is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from steps 1 and 2 without deciding it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about the non-Jewish זבה who converted stays unresolved (תיקו).

steps.title: שמואל: a זב needs enough discharge to seal the opening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'they make impure in any amount.' Then שמואל says a זב is only impure from enough discharge to seal the opening of the organ, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And they make impure in any amount.' שמואל said: A זב needs enough discharge to seal the opening of the organ, as it says: 'or his flesh is sealed from his discharge.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule and then brings שמואל's minimum amount for a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says זוב makes one impure in any amount. שמואל instead requires a minimum: enough to seal the opening. His source is the word 'החתים' (sealed) in the פסוק. This creates an obvious tension with the משנה, which the next step will raise.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who has a זיבה discharge, which makes him impure.
In any amount at all, even the smallest.
The sealing of the opening of the organ. It is a minimum amount of discharge.
'Was sealed' or 'was stopped.' This is the word in the פסוק that שמואל uses.

phrases.english: "And they make impure in any amount."
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה. They are about זוב and שכבת זרע.

phrases.english: שמואל said:
A זב needs enough to seal the opening of the organ,
as it says:
"Or his flesh is sealed from his discharge."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, unconnected to the תיקו before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, a זב becomes impure only from enough discharge to seal the opening of the organ.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה says any amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from the משנה, which says זוב makes one impure in any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: 'They make impure in any amount'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's minimum amount by pointing to the משנה's clear words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'any amount,' which means there is no minimum at all. That directly contradicts שמואל, who requires enough to seal the opening.

keyTerms.meaning: They make impure.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
"They make impure in any amount"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's rule from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a זב needs enough to seal the opening.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה clearly says any amount makes one impure, so there is no minimum.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי נתן, whose view the חכמים rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל follows a ברייתא in which רבי נתן, quoting רבי ישמעאל, requires the sealing amount. The חכמים did not agree, and the משנה follows them.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said it following רבי נתן. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says in the name of רבי ישמעאל: A זב needs enough to seal the opening of the organ. But they did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל is not making up a new view. He follows an older תנא, רבי נתן, whose opinion differs from the one behind the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction is solved by showing this is an older argument between תנאים. The משנה follows the חכמים, who say any amount counts. שמואל follows רבי נתן in the name of רבי ישמעאל, who requires the sealing amount, even though the חכמים 'did not agree with him.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'He said it following...' This means the אמורא is following one side of an older argument.
In the name of.
'And they did not agree with him.' The other חכמים rejected his view.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (the חכמים) says any amount of זוב makes one impure. שמואל follows רבי נתן in the name of רבי ישמעאל, who requires enough to seal the opening. The חכמים did not accept that view.

phrases.english: He said it following רבי נתן,
phrases.notes: 'He' is שמואל.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: רבי נתן says in the name of רבי ישמעאל:
A זב needs enough to seal the opening of the organ,
and they did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that שמואל follows a תנא who disagrees with the opinion behind the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that שמואל was contradicting the משנה with no support.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי נתן in the name of רבי ישמעאל, while the משנה follows the חכמים who rejected that view.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי ישמעאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי ישמעאל's source and answers that it is the phrase 'או החתים בשרו מזובו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי ישמעאל's reason? Because the פסוק says: 'or his flesh is sealed from his discharge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי ישמעאל gets his rule that a זב needs enough discharge to seal the opening of the organ. It answers with a phrase from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'החתים בשרו' mean the flesh is sealed or blocked by the discharge. רבי ישמעאל reads this as the minimum amount: only a discharge big enough to seal the opening counts. This explains the source of the opinion that שמואל follows.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason, meaning what is the source
A פסוק from the Torah
Sealed or blocked up
The discharge that makes a man a זב

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי ישמעאל?
Because the verse says:
"Or his flesh is sealed from his discharge."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 said שמואל follows רבי ישמעאל; now the גמרא gives רבי ישמעאל's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for requiring a sealing amount of discharge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'או החתים בשרו מזובו' shows the discharge must be enough to seal the organ.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from that phrase?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'החתים בשרו' to teach that only a moist discharge makes impure, not a dry one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They need that phrase for something else: a moist discharge makes impure, and a dry one does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן, who do not require a sealing amount, do with that same phrase. It answers that they use it to teach a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every phrase in the Torah must teach something, so the רבנן need a use for 'החתים'. They learn from it that only a moist discharge (the kind that could seal) makes impure, while a dry one does not. So they agree the phrase teaches something about the discharge, just not a minimum amount.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for a different teaching
Moist, wet
Dry
Makes impure

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what do the רבנן do with this phrase, since they don't learn the sealing amount from it?

phrases.english: They need that phrase for this:
A moist discharge makes impure, but a dry one does not make impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבי ישמעאל's source, the גמרא asks how the other side uses the same words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן use the phrase 'או החתים בשרו מזובו'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that only a moist discharge makes impure, not a dry one.

steps.title: Where does רבי ישמעאל learn the moist rule?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns that only a moist discharge makes impure from the word 'רר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? He learns that rule from the word 'רר' (flows).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the reverse: רבי ישמעאל also agrees that a dry discharge does not make impure, so where does he learn it? It answers: from the word 'רר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי ישמעאל used 'החתים' for the sealing amount, he needs a different source for the moist rule. The word 'רר' means flowing, and only something moist can flow. So both sides hold the moist rule; they just learn it from different words.

keyTerms.meaning: Flows, runs (like a liquid)
It comes out from, it is learned from

phrases.english: And רבי ישמעאל?
phrases.notes: Meaning: where does he learn that a dry discharge doesn't make impure?

phrases.english: That is learned from "flows."
phrases.notes: From the same פסוק: 'רר בשרו את זובו', his flesh flows with his discharge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבנן's use of 'החתים' raises the question of where רבי ישמעאל gets the moist rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי ישמעאל's source for the rule that only moist discharge makes impure.

steps.title: The רבנן use the words to count three sightings
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'רר' to count three mentions of discharge, teaching that a זב with three sightings must bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? That word comes for counting: 'his discharge' is one, 'his flesh flows' is two, 'with his discharge' is three. This teaches that a זב who had three sightings is obligated to bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the word 'רר', and answers that it is part of a count of three. The next step continues the רבנן's reading of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the discharge three times: 'בזובו', 'רר בשרו', and 'את זובו'. The רבנן count these as three sightings and learn that a זב with three sightings must bring a קרבן. Since 'רר' is needed for the count, the רבנן cannot use it for the moist rule, which is why they learned that from 'החתים'.

keyTerms.meaning: For counting, to give a number
Sightings, times a discharge was seen
An offering brought in the בית המקדש
A man who has become impure through a discharge

steps.whatToRemember: Every phrase in the פסוק has a job. רבי ישמעאל: 'החתים' = sealing amount, 'רר' = moist only. רבנן: 'החתים' = moist only, 'רר' = part of the count of three sightings for a קרבן.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what do they do with the word 'רר'?

phrases.english: That word comes for counting:
"His discharge" is one,
phrases.notes: This is the first part of the פסוק: 'טמאתו בזובו', his impurity in his discharge.

phrases.english: "His flesh flows" is two,
"With his discharge" is three,

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל זָב בַּעַל שָׁלֹשׁ רְאִיּוֹת
phrases.english: It teaches about a זב who had three sightings
That he is obligated to bring an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing רבי ישמעאל uses 'רר' for the moist rule, the גמרא shows the רבנן need 'רר' for something else.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן use the word 'רר'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is part of a count of three mentions of discharge, teaching that a זב with three sightings brings a קרבן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both sides find a use for every phrase of the פסוק; the disagreement about the sealing amount comes down to which phrase teaches which rule.

steps.title: The end of the verse teaches that two sightings already make a bed and seat impure
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read 'מזובו' as 'part of his discharge.' This teaches that a זב with only two sightings already makes a משכב and מושב impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or his flesh be stopped from his issue, he is impure': even part of his issue makes him impure. This teaches that a זב who had two sightings makes a bed and a seat impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining how the רבנן read the rest of the פסוק. The small word 'מזובו' means 'from part of his discharge.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 the רבנן counted three mentions of discharge to require a קרבן. Here they add that the extra letter מ in 'מזובו' means 'part of.' So even 'part' of the full three, meaning two sightings, is enough to make him a source of טומאה for a bed and a seat.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of; some of
A זב who had two sightings of discharge
A bed (something made to lie on) and a seat (something made to sit on)

steps.confusionAlert: Two sightings already make him fully impure, including making his bed and seat impure. Only the קרבן needs three sightings.

phrases.english: "Or his flesh be stopped from his issue, impure":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:3

phrases.english: even part of his issue makes impure,

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת
phrases.english: it teaches about a זב who had two sightings
that he makes a bed and a seat impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבנן's reading of the פסוק that began in Steps 8 and 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'מזובו' (part of his discharge) teaches that two sightings already bring impurity of משכב ומושב.

steps.title: Where does רבי ישמעאל learn the number of sightings?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל used 'החתים' for the sealing rule, so the גמרא asks where he learns the number of sightings. Answer: from רבי סימאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל, where does he learn the number of sightings from? He learns it from רבי סימאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי ישמעאל knows the rules about two and three sightings. It answers briefly that he follows רבי סימאי, which sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן learned the counting from the words in ויקרא 15:3. רבי ישמעאל cannot do that, because he already used 'החתים' to teach the sealing amount (Step 7). So he needs another source for the counting.

keyTerms.meaning: The count, meaning the number of sightings needed
From where does he know it?
He learns it from

phrases.english: And רבי ישמעאל,
where does he learn the count from?
He learns it from the teaching of רבי סימאי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to רבי ישמעאל and asks for his source for what the רבנן just derived.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי ישמעאל's source for two sightings for טומאה and three for a קרבן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns it from רבי סימאי.

steps.title: רבי סימאי: two sightings for impurity, three for the offering
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק counts two mentions of discharge and calls him impure. Another counts three and also calls him impure. So two are for טומאה and three are for the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי סימאי says, the Torah counted two and called him 'impure,' and it counted three and called him 'impure.' How does this fit together? Two are for impurity, and three are for the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי סימאי that it just mentioned. It shows how the counting comes from comparing two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 15:2 mentions discharge twice ('זב' and 'זובו') and says 'טמא.' ויקרא 15:3 mentions it three times and also says 'טמא.' Since two would be enough for impurity, the third must be for something extra: the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah counted (mentions of discharge)
How is this? (how do the two פסוקים fit together)
The offering a זב brings after becoming pure

steps.whatToRemember: According to everyone, two sightings make a זב impure and three require a קרבן. The only argument is which words of the Torah teach it.

phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי סימאי says:
The Torah counted two and called him "impure,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:2

phrases.english: and it counted three and called him "impure."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:3

phrases.english: How is this?
Two are for impurity, and three are for the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the source of רבי סימאי mentioned in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two sightings make a זב impure, and three sightings require a קרבן.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from 'איש איש כי יהיה זב מבשרו'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn both rules from 15:3, so the גמרא asks what 15:2 teaches them. Answer: the discharge must come out of his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who learns both rules from 'This shall be his impurity in his issue,' what does he do with 'When any man has an issue out of his flesh'? He needs it to teach that the discharge must come out of his flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with ויקרא 15:2, since they did not use it for counting. It answers that it teaches the discharge must actually leave the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי סימאי needed 15:2 for the count of two. The רבנן got both two and three from 15:3, so 15:2 seemed free. They use the word 'מבשרו' to teach that he is impure only once the discharge comes out of his flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them (both rules: impurity and the קרבן)
What does he do with it? (what does he learn from this פסוק)
He needs it for (it teaches something else)

phrases.english: And according to the one who learns both
phrases.notes: This means the רבנן, who learned both two and three sightings from the same פסוק.

phrases.english: from "This shall be his impurity in his issue,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:3

phrases.english: "When any man has an issue out of his flesh"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:2

phrases.english: what does he do with it?
He needs it to teach: not until it comes out of his flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי סימאי used 15:2 for counting, the גמרא asks what the רבנן use it for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from ויקרא 15:2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: That a זב is impure only once the discharge comes out of his flesh.

steps.title: Why does the Torah say 'זובו טמא'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the words 'his issue is impure' are needed. Answer: the discharge itself is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'his issue is impure'? It teaches about the discharge, that it itself is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the extra words 'זובו טמא' teach. It answers that the discharge itself is a source of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the man becomes impure. These words add that the discharge itself is impure. So it can make other things impure when they touch it.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (why does the Torah write this)
The discharge of a זב

steps.whatToRemember: From these פסוקים we learn: two sightings bring טומאה, three bring a קרבן, the discharge must leave the body, and the discharge itself is impure.

phrases.english: "His issue is impure": why do I need it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:2

phrases.english: It teaches about the discharge, that it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the words of ויקרא 15:2 and moves to its last words.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The discharge itself is impure and can make other things impure.

steps.title: Any amount for the man it comes from, a lentil-size for one who touches
steps.stepSummary: רב חנילאי, in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, splits the measure of שכבת זרע. Any amount makes impure the man it comes out of. A person who touches it needs a כעדשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנילאי said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: שכבת זרע makes the man who emits it impure in any amount. Someone who touches it becomes impure only if it is the size of a lentil.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule is stated about how much שכבת זרע is needed to cause טומאה. The amount depends on whether you are the man it came from or someone touching it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different people here. The man it comes out of (רואה) becomes impure from even a tiny amount. Someone else who touches it (נוגע) needs a lentil-size piece, the same minimum as a שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Semen, a source of טומאה
The one who 'sees' it, meaning the man it comes out of
Someone who touches it
The size of a lentil, a minimum amount for טומאה
Any amount at all, even tiny

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חֲנִילַאי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rav Chanilai said in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
Semen: for the one who emits it, in any amount;
phrases.notes: Literally 'the one who sees.' He means the man whose body it comes out of.

phrases.english: for one who touches it, a lentil-size.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנִילַאי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the משנה's rule that semen makes impure in any amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Semen makes the man who emits it impure in any amount. One who touches it needs a lentil-size.

steps.title: The משנה says any amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חנילאי from the משנה. The משנה says semen makes impure בכל שהן, and that seems to include someone who touches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה that they make impure in any amount! Isn't that talking about someone who touches it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new rule using our משנה, which says semen makes impure in any amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives no minimum at all. If it means someone who touches it, that contradicts רב חנילאי's lentil-size rule for a נוגע.

keyTerms.meaning: In any amount whatsoever
'Isn't it…?', a way of suggesting how to read a source

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: "they make impure in any amount"!
phrases.notes: This is our משנה, talking about the discharge of a זב and semen.

phrases.english: Is it not referring to one who touches?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מימרא of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lentil-size rule for a נוגע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives no minimum, and that seems to include someone who touches.

steps.title: The משנה means the man it comes from
steps.stepSummary: The answer is no: the משנה is talking about the רואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the man who emits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's 'any amount' is only about the man it comes out of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנילאי also agrees that the רואה becomes impure from any amount. So the משנה matches him, and the lentil-size rule for a נוגע still stands.

phrases.english: No, it refers to the one who emits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'any amount' includes one who touches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about the man it comes out of.

steps.title: A ברייתא comparing semen and a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing how semen is stricter than a שרץ and how a שרץ is stricter than semen. One point is that semen makes impure בכל שהוא. The גמרא asks if that means someone who touches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: semen is stricter than a שרץ in one way, and a שרץ is stricter than semen in another way. A שרץ is stricter because its טומאה is not divided, which is not true of semen. Semen is stricter because it makes impure in any amount, which is not true of a שרץ. Isn't this talking about someone who touches it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge, this time from a ברייתא, against the lentil-size rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרץ makes impure only by touch and needs a lentil-size. The ברייתא says semen is stricter because any amount makes impure. Since the comparison is with touching a שרץ, it seems to mean touching semen too, which would contradict רב חנילאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency, a way one thing is stricter than another
A dead creeping creature that makes impure
Its טומאה is not divided, meaning it always works the same way
Which is not the case with…

phrases.english: Come and hear:
There is a stringency in semen beyond a creeping creature,
and a stringency in a creeping creature beyond semen.
The stringency in a creeping creature:
that a creeping creature's impurity is not divided,
which is not so with semen.
The stringency in semen:
that semen makes impure in any amount,
which is not so with a creeping creature.
Is it not referring to one who touches?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: חוֹמֶר בְּשִׁכְבַת זֶרַע מִבְּשֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to step 16, this time from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lentil-size rule for a נוגע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says semen makes impure in any amount, unlike a שרץ. That seems to mean touching it.

steps.title: The ברייתא also means the man it comes from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: the ברייתא is talking about the רואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the man who emits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its answer: the ברייתא's 'any amount' is only about the man it comes out of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the ברייתא does not say anything about a נוגע. So רב חנילאי's lentil-size rule is not contradicted.

phrases.english: No, it refers to the one who emits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'any amount' is about touching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the man it comes out of.

steps.title: But the ברייתא compares it to a שרץ, which is about touching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The ברייתא sets semen side by side with a שרץ, and a שרץ makes impure by נגיעה. So semen in the ברייתא should also be about touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches semen as similar to a שרץ. Just as a שרץ makes impure by touch, semen here must also be about touch!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. It points out that the ברייתא's comparison suggests both cases are about touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרץ never makes impure by 'seeing.' It only makes impure by touch. If the ברייתא compares the two, it seems both should be about the same kind of contact, so 'any amount' would apply to a נוגע.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, parallel with
Touching, contact
It teaches

phrases.english: But it teaches it as similar to a creeping creature;
just as a creeping creature is by contact,
so too semen is by contact!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about the רואה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parallel with a שרץ, which makes impure only by touch, implies the semen case is also about touch.

steps.title: The ברייתא compares the categories in general
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the ברייתא compares 'שם שרץ' and 'שם שכבת זרע' as general types of טומאה. It does not mean they make impure in the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: the ברייתא is talking about the category of שרץ and the category of semen in general.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה defends the answer. He says the ברייתא is only comparing the two types of טומאה in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists strict points of each type of טומאה. It does not claim both work through touch. So the 'any amount' point can be about the רואה, and רב חנילאי's lentil-size rule for a נוגע stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'name'; the general category

steps.whatToRemember: Semen makes the man it comes out of impure in any amount. Someone who touches it needs a lentil-size. The משנה and the ברייתא that say 'any amount' are both about the man it comes out of.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
It teaches the category of a creeping creature,
and it teaches the category of semen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: שׁוּם שֶׁרֶץ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the comparison as general, not about how impurity is passed on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since semen is compared to a שרץ, both must be about touching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only compares the two categories of טומאה in general, so the semen point can be about the רואה.

steps.title: Does a creeping animal really need a lentil-size to make impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that a שרץ does not make impure בכל שהוא. A משנה says a whole limb of a שרץ makes impure even when it is smaller than a lentil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does a שרץ really not make impure in any amount? But we learned in a משנה: limbs have no minimum size. Even less than a כזית of a corpse, less than a כזית of a נבלה, or less than a כעדשה of a שרץ makes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's point that a שרץ needs a lentil-size to make impure. It quotes a משנה showing a שרץ limb can make impure even when it is smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said semen is stricter because it makes impure בכל שהוא, while a שרץ needs a כעדשה. The משנה in אהלות says a whole limb has no minimum size, even for a שרץ. So it looks like a שרץ can also make impure in a tiny amount.

keyTerms.meaning: In any amount at all, even the smallest bit
Limbs. Here it means whole limbs, with bone, flesh and sinew
A minimum size needed for a law to apply
Olive-size, the usual minimum for a corpse or a נבלה
Lentil-size, the usual minimum for a שרץ
An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: And does a creeping animal not make impure in any amount?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא from step 19, which said only semen makes impure בכל שהוא, while a שרץ needs a lentil-size.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
phrases.notes: אהלות 1:7

phrases.english: Limbs have no minimum measure,
less than an olive-bulk of a corpse's flesh,
and less than an olive-bulk of a carcass's flesh,
and less than a lentil-bulk of a creeping animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the semen side of the ברייתא to its claim about the minimum size of a שרץ
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that a שרץ needs a כעדשה and does not make impure בכל שהוא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says a whole שרץ limb smaller than a lentil still makes impure, so a שרץ can make impure in any amount

steps.title: A whole limb counts as a lentil-size
steps.stepSummary: A whole limb is different: being complete makes it count as a כעדשה. The proof is that if even a little were missing, it would not make impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A limb is different, because when it is whole it stands in place of a lentil-size. The proof: if a little bit of the limb were missing, would it make impure? No.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the limb case is a special exception. A whole limb is treated as if it were a full lentil-size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limb makes impure because it is complete, not because size doesn't matter for a שרץ. The proof is that a limb missing even a little does not make impure. So the ברייתא's rule stands: ordinary שרץ flesh still needs a כעדשה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different, used to show a case is an exception
It stands in place of a lentil-size, it counts as one
A little bit

steps.whatToRemember: A whole limb of a שרץ makes impure because it is complete. It counts like a lentil-size even if it is smaller, but once a bit is missing it no longer makes impure.

phrases.english: A limb is different,
since the whole of it stands in place of a lentil-bulk,
for if it were missing a little bit,
would the limb make impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה about limbs
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a whole limb is a special exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The limb rule shows a שרץ makes impure in any amount
steps.terutzMaskana: A whole limb is treated as a full כעדשה; ordinary שרץ flesh still needs a lentil-size

steps.title: What does 'divided impurity' of semen mean?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא said a שרץ is stricter because its impurity is not divided, unlike semen. The גמרא asks what this division in semen is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Semen, whose impurity is divided: what is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another line of the ברייתא and asks what it means. This sets up the next steps, where an answer is suggested and tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed as a stringency of שרץ that its impurity is not 'divided', while semen's is. The גמרא wants to know in what way semen's impurity is split into cases that make impure and cases that don't.

keyTerms.meaning: Its impurity is divided: some kinds make impure and some do not
What is it? A request to explain what something means

phrases.english: Semen, whose impurity is divided —
what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a different point in the same ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the 'division' in the impurity of semen refers to

steps.title: Not Jews versus non-Jews, because a שרץ has a split too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the split is between the semen of Jews and of non-Jews. It rejects this because a שרץ also has a split: a sea mouse is not impure, but a land mouse is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the split is between Jews and non-Jews, then a שרץ has a split too: a sea mouse and a land mouse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one explanation and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'divided' meant Jews versus non-Jews, the ברייתא could not say a שרץ has no division. A mouse also splits: a land mouse makes impure and a sea mouse does not. So this kind of split cannot be what makes semen different.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, used to bring a suggestion that will be tested
There is the same thing here too
A sea mouse, a sea creature called a mouse, which is not impure

phrases.english: If you say: between Jews and non-Jews,
there is the same thing here too:
a sea mouse and a land mouse!
phrases.notes: Only the land mouse is one of the impure creeping animals, so a שרץ has a split too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to step 25's question and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that 'divided' means Jews versus non-Jews
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A שרץ has a matching split (sea mouse versus land mouse), so this cannot be what sets semen apart

steps.title: The split is between a minor and an adult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that semen's 'divided impurity' means the difference between a קטן and a גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the split is between a minor and an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer: semen's impurity depends on whether the man is a minor or an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor's emission is not considered semen and does not make impure, but an adult's does. A שרץ has no such split by age or size, so the ברייתא's contrast works.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, brings the correct answer after rejecting another
A minor, before adulthood
An adult

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'divided impurity' of semen means minor versus adult. A שרץ makes impure no matter how young or small it is.

phrases.english: Rather, between a minor and an adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after the first suggestion was rejected
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The division is between the emission of a קטן, which does not make impure, and that of a גדול, which does

steps.title: רב פפא: the toucher's amount is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the amount of semen that makes a toucher טמא is a תנאים dispute. He quotes the source that teaches touching semen makes one טמא: the words "או איש".
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is like a dispute of תנאים. From where do we learn that someone who touches semen is also טמא? The verse says "or a man".
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new point: the size of semen needed to make a person who touches it טמא is a disagreement among תנאים. He starts by quoting the source for the rule that touching semen makes one טמא, setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's main case of semen impurity is the man who emits it. The ברייתא learns from the extra words "או איש" that touching semen also makes one טמא, by linking it to the nearby case of touching a שרץ. Because touching semen is learned from שרץ, the question becomes how many of the שרץ's rules come along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: "Like the תנאים": this question is already a disagreement among the תנאים
To include: to add another case from a word in the verse
One who touches
Semen
"The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק used as the source

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב חנילאי's lentil-size rule for one who touches semen is not agreed by everyone. For the toucher, the amount depends on a תנאים dispute.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is like a dispute of tannaim,
From where do we include one who touches semen?
The verse says: "Or a man."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:5. The next words there talk about touching a שרץ, which is how semen gets linked to שרץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב חנילאי's rule (step 16) and shows that the amount of semen needed to make a toucher טמא is itself a תנאים dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touching semen makes one טמא, learned from "או איש", which links it to touching a שרץ. The required amount depends on a תנאים dispute.

steps.title: The general dispute: copy everything, or keep the case in its own place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names a general disagreement among תנאים about learning one law from another. One view copies all the source's details; the other borrows only the main point and keeps the rest from the case's own rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנאים disagree in general. Some say: learn from it, and learn from it again (copy all its details). Others say: learn from it, but leave the new case in its own place (keep its own details).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a general rule-dispute about how far a comparison reaches. This sets up the next two steps, which apply each view to semen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When law B is learned from law A, one view says B takes on all of A's details too (דון מינה ומינה). The other view says B borrows only the main point from A, and its other details come from B's own rules (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה).

keyTerms.meaning: In general: this dispute shows up in other places, not only here
"Learn from it, and from it": the new case copies all the details of the source case
"Learn from it, but set it in its own place": borrow only the main point, and keep the new case's own details

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that touching semen makes one טמא. They only argue about which details come along with that rule, here the amount.

phrases.english: And tannaim disagree in general,
for there are those who say:
Infer from it, and from it,
phrases.notes: Literally "judge from it and from it": you take the main rule and its details from the same source.

phrases.english: and there are those who say:
Infer from it, but establish it in its own place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the תנאים dispute mentioned by רב פפא actually is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two general approaches to a comparison: copy all the details (דון מינה ומינה), or borrow only the main point (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה).

steps.title: First view: semen for a toucher needs a lentil-size, like a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: Under דון מינה ומינה, semen copies the שרץ in two ways. It makes impure by touching, and only in the amount of a כעדשה (lentil-size).
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the view "learn from it and from it": just as a שרץ makes impure by touching, so does semen. And from it again: just as a שרץ needs a lentil-size, so semen needs a lentil-size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the first view to our case. Semen learns everything from the שרץ, including its minimum size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first lesson from שרץ is that touching semen makes one טמא. Because this view copies all the details, it also takes the שרץ's lentil-size minimum. So under this view, a tiny bit of semen does not make a toucher טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping creature whose dead body makes one טמא
Touching
The size of a lentil: the minimum amount of a שרץ that makes one טמא

phrases.english: According to the one who says "infer from it and from it":
just as a sheretz makes impure by touching,
so too semen makes impure by touching;
and "from it" again:
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the rule: now we take a detail, the amount, from the שרץ too.

phrases.english: just as a sheretz makes impure in the amount of a lentil,
so too semen makes impure in the amount of a lentil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the first general view from the previous step to touching semen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under דון מינה ומינה, semen makes a toucher טמא only in the amount of a כעדשה, like a שרץ.

steps.title: Second view: semen for a toucher counts in any amount
steps.stepSummary: Under דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, semen borrows only the idea of touching from the שרץ. Its amount stays as semen's own rule: just as the one who emits it is טמא with any amount (משהו), so is the one who touches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the view "learn from it but keep it in its place": just as a שרץ makes impure by touching, so does semen. But keep it in its own place: just as semen makes the one who emits it טמא with any tiny amount, so it makes the one who touches it טמא with any tiny amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the second view to our case. This finishes רב פפא's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view borrows only the basic rule, that touching makes one טמא, from the שרץ. The amount comes from semen's own laws, where even a tiny bit makes the one who emits it טמא. So under this view a toucher also becomes טמא with a tiny amount, unlike רב חנילאי's lentil-size rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "one who sees": here, the man who emits the semen
Any tiny amount at all

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's two sides: under דון מינה ומינה, a toucher needs a כעדשה, like a שרץ, which matches רב חנילאי. Under דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, a toucher becomes טמא with a משהו, like the one who emits it.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְּאַתְרַהּ,
phrases.english: And according to the one who says "infer from it, but establish it in its own place":
just as a sheretz makes impure by touching,
so too semen makes impure by touching,
but establish it in its own place:
just as semen makes the one who emits it impure with any amount,
so too it makes the one who touches it impure with any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְּאַתְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the dispute, opposite to the lentil-size view in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, semen makes a toucher טמא in any amount (משהו), just as it does for the one who emits it.

steps.title: Maybe the source is semen's own verse, not the שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רב פפא: perhaps the ברייתא learns touching semen from the semen פסוק itself. If so, everyone would agree the amount is משהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן said to רב פפא: How do you know the ברייתא learns this from the "or whoever" said about a שרץ? Maybe it learns it from "or whoever the flow of seed goes out from him." Then everyone would say we copy everything from that source.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן attacks the basic assumption behind רב פפא's claim that this is a תנאים dispute. He suggests a different source verse for the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said the words "או איש" come from the שרץ verse, so the two views on borrowing laws give different amounts. But if "או איש" is from the semen verse itself, the source and the case are the same topic. Then even under דון מינה ומינה we copy semen's own amount, משהו, and the dispute between the תנאים disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know?
Perhaps, maybe
He is including it, drawing it in from a verse
According to everyone
Semen, a flow of seed

steps.confusionAlert: Both verses contain the words "או איש", one right after the other. The whole argument is about which "או איש" the ברייתא is reading.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan, said to Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּאי דְּמֵ״אוֹ אִישׁ״ דְּשֶׁרֶץ קָמְרַבֵּי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: From where do you know that he includes it from the "or whoever" of the creeping animal?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:5. This is the verse about touching a שרץ.

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא מֵ״אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָרַע״
phrases.english: Perhaps it is from "or whoever the flow of seed goes out from him"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4

phrases.english: that he includes it,
and according to everyone, we learn from it and copy all its details from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּמֵ״אוֹ אִישׁ״ דְּשֶׁרֶץ קָמְרַבֵּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source reading that steps 28-31 were built on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the toucher's amount is a תנאים dispute based on the שרץ verse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "או איש" comes from the semen verse, there is no outside source, so both views of borrowing give the same result, משהו.

steps.title: The reciters had both versions
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis asked the reciters of the ברייתות. Some taught the ברייתא in a way that fits רב פפא, and some in a way that fits רב הונא בריה דרב נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked the reciters. Some taught it like רב פפא, and some taught it like רב הונא son of רב נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question by checking how the ברייתא was actually recited. It found that both readings existed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not decided by logic but by checking the text itself. Since the reciters disagreed on which verse the ברייתא uses, both רב פפא's view and רב הונא's view have textual support. The question is left with two valid versions.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked them
Here: the reciters who memorized and repeated משניות and ברייתות
There are those who teach (recite) it

steps.whatToRemember: The amount of semen that makes a toucher טמא depends on the source verse. If it comes from the שרץ verse, the תנאים argue (כעדשה or משהו). If it comes from the semen verse, everyone says משהו. Both versions of the ברייתא were taught.
steps.confusionAlert: Here תנאי does not mean the sages of the משנה era. It means the people whose job was to recite the ברייתות from memory.

phrases.english: They asked the reciters of the teachings,
there are those who teach it like Rav Pappa,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיכָּא דְּתָנֵי כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן.
phrases.english: and there are those who teach it like Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 32's challenge by checking how the ברייתא was recited.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both readings of the ברייתא exist, so both רב פפא's and רב הונא's understandings are supported.

steps.title: A newborn girl can become נדה and זבה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that a one-day-old girl can become טמאה as a נדה, and a ten-day-old girl can become a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A baby girl one day old becomes טמאה as a נדה. A girl ten days old becomes טמאה with זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a baby girl has the impurity laws of a grown woman from her first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a newborn who sees blood is a נדה. זיבה needs blood on three days outside the seven days of נדה. So the earliest a girl can become a זבה is at ten days old: seven days of נדה plus three more days.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the opening of a new משנה
A baby girl
A woman who is טמאה from her monthly flow
Impurity of a זבה, from blood seen outside the days of נדה

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A baby girl one day old
becomes impure as a menstruating woman.
A girl ten days old
becomes impure with zivah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' תִּנוֹקֶת בַּת יוֹם אֶחָד מִטַּמְּאָה בְּנִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby girl becomes a נדה from day one and a זבה from day ten.

steps.title: A newborn boy can become טמא in three ways
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists that a one-day-old boy becomes טמא as a זב, through נגעים, and through contact with a dead body.
steps.simpleTranslation: A baby boy one day old becomes טמא with זיבה, becomes טמא with נגעים, and becomes טמא with the impurity of a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a baby boy and begins a long list of adult laws that already apply to him on his first day. This step covers the impurity laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy does not need to wait like a girl does, so he can become a זב right away. His skin can also become טמא from נגעים, and he becomes טמא from a dead body just like an adult.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby boy
Skin marks of צרעת that make a person טמא
Impurity from a dead body

phrases.english: A baby boy one day old
becomes impure with zivah,
and becomes impure with leprous marks,
and becomes impure with the impurity of a corpse,

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּנוֹק בֶּן יוֹם אֶחָד מִטַּמֵּא בְּזִיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from a baby girl to a baby boy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From day one, a baby boy can become טמא through זיבה, נגעים and a dead body.

steps.title: A newborn boy already affects יבום and תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: a one-day-old boy can create or cancel a יבום obligation, and can let his mother eat תרומה or stop her from eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He ties a widow to יבום, he exempts from יבום, he lets someone eat תרומה, and he disqualifies someone from תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing what a newborn boy does. Now it moves from impurity to family laws: יבום and eating תרומה. The list continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A living son counts as a son from his first day. So if his brother dies childless, the widow is tied to him for יבום. If his father dies, his mother is free from יבום because there is a child. His existence also decides whether his mother may eat תרומה after his father is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Ties a childless widow to him for יבום
Frees a widow from יבום because the dead man has a child
Allows someone to eat תרומה
Takes away someone's right to eat תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: The baby is not the one eating or losing תרומה here. He affects his mother's right to eat it, depending on whether his father was a כהן or a ישראל.

phrases.english: and he ties a widow to levirate marriage,
and he exempts from levirate marriage,
and he lets her eat teruma,
phrases.notes: 'Her' is his mother: a ישראלית whose כהן husband died may keep eating תרומה because of this son.

phrases.english: and he disqualifies her from teruma,
phrases.notes: Some versions have אֶת, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is מִן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list about a one-day-old boy, moving from טומאה to יבום and תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From day one, a baby boy counts as a son for the laws of יבום and for his mother's right to eat תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a son counts as a full son from birth for family laws, even though he cannot do anything himself.
